writtenTo: The new generation of Israel about to enter the Promised Land
importantNotes: Deuteronomy means 'second law' — it's a restatement of the Law for the new generation.
The Shema (Deut 6:4-5) is the central confession of faith in Judaism.
Jesus quoted Deuteronomy three times when tempted by Satan (Matt 4).
Deuteronomy is one of the most quoted OT books in the New Testament.
Moses dies at the end of the book, having seen but not entered the Promised Land.

chapters.1: Moses recounts the journey from Horeb to Kadesh Barnea and the appointment of leaders.
chapters.2: Israel's journey through Edom, Moab, and Ammon; victory over King Sihon.
chapters.3: Victory over King Og of Bashan; the land east of the Jordan is distributed.
chapters.4: Moses urges obedience to God's commands; warning against idolatry.
chapters.5: Moses restates the Ten Commandments to the new generation.
chapters.6: The Shema — 'Love the LORD your God with all your heart'; teach God's words to your children.
chapters.7: Instructions for conquering Canaan; Israel is chosen as God's treasured people.
chapters.8: Remember the LORD in prosperity; do not forget Him when you are blessed.
chapters.9: Israel's stubbornness recalled — the golden calf incident and other rebellions.
chapters.10: New tablets of stone; what God requires — to fear, love, and serve Him.
chapters.11: Love and obey God; the blessings of the Promised Land depend on faithfulness.
chapters.12: Worship only at the place God chooses; destroy all pagan worship sites.
chapters.13: Warnings against following false prophets and those who entice you to idolatry.
chapters.14: Clean and unclean foods; laws about tithing.
chapters.15: The year of release for debts; generosity toward the poor; firstborn animals.
chapters.16: The three annual feasts — Passover, Weeks, and Tabernacles; justice and judges.
chapters.17: Laws about kings, worship, and capital cases; the king must read God's law.
chapters.18: Provisions for Levites; the promise of a prophet like Moses (fulfilled in Christ).
chapters.19: Cities of refuge; laws about witnesses; boundaries.
chapters.20: Rules of warfare — trust in God, not in military strength.
chapters.21: Laws about unsolved murders, captive women, rebellious sons, and burial.
chapters.22: Various laws about lost property, clothing, building safety, and sexual morality.
chapters.23: Laws about the assembly, camp cleanliness, escaped slaves, and vows.
chapters.24: Laws about divorce, justice for the vulnerable, and gleaning for the poor.
chapters.25: Laws about fair punishment, levirate marriage, and honest weights and measures.
chapters.26: Firstfruits and tithes offered with gratitude; covenant affirmation.
chapters.27: The altar on Mount Ebal; the curses proclaimed from Mount Ebal.
chapters.28: Blessings for obedience and curses for disobedience — a pivotal chapter.
chapters.29: Renewal of the covenant on the plains of Moab.
chapters.30: The choice between life and death — 'choose life' that you may live.
chapters.31: Moses commissions Joshua; the Law is entrusted to the Levites.
chapters.32: The Song of Moses — a poetic summary of God's faithfulness and Israel's unfaithfulness.
chapters.33: Moses blesses each of the twelve tribes of Israel.
chapters.34: Moses views the Promised Land from Mount Nebo and dies; Joshua takes over leadership.
